# How to use Claude Artifacts to create and preview your work

By the end of this guide, you'll be able to ask Claude, the helpful AI assistant, to produce documents, summaries, or even a tiny web app and see the result instantly in your conversation. This is for anyone who wants a quick, visual way to turn ideas into finished pieces without needing any coding experience.

## Before you start
-   **An Anthropic account:** You'll need a login to access Claude. If you don't have one, you can usually sign up for free on the Claude website.
-   **A modern web browser on a desktop or laptop:** While Claude works on mobile, the Artifacts feature is best viewed and used on a larger screen like a computer or tablet.
-   **An idea or a piece of text:** Think of something you'd like Claude to help you create, like a thank-you letter, a summary of an article, or a simple list.
-   **Rough total time:** Allow about 5-10 minutes to follow this guide for the first time. The Artifacts feature is generally available on Claude's free tier.

## Step 1 — Open Claude and start a new chat
First, open your web browser and go to `claude.ai`. You'll either land on the login page or, if you're already logged in, Claude's main interface. Once you're in, look for a button to start a fresh conversation. This button is typically in the top-left corner of the screen and might be labeled "+ New chat" or simply have a "+" icon. Click it to open a blank slate for your new request.

**If it looks different:** The "New chat" button might appear as a pencil icon, a speech bubble, or a clear text link. Just look for an option that clearly indicates starting a fresh conversation.

**💬 Example:** You see a button in the sidebar labeled "+ New chat".

**You'll know it worked when** you see a blank chat conversation area ready for your input, often with a greeting from Claude like "Hello! How can I help you today?"

## Step 2 — Write a prompt that asks for an artifact
Claude's Artifacts appear automatically when you ask for content that can be displayed as a document, code, or visual item. You don't need to enable a special pane — just write your request. In the message box at the bottom of the chat window, type your request and include a word that signals you want an artifact, like "create," "generate," or "make."

**If it looks different:** The message box will always be at the very bottom of the chat, usually labeled "Message Claude..." or "Type your message here."

**💬 Example:**
```
Create a thank-you letter artifact for my neighbour, Emma, who helped me move my sofa on Saturday. Use a friendly tone and keep it under 200 words.
```

**You'll know it worked when** you press Enter or click the "Send" button (often a paper plane icon), and Claude starts generating a response. The artifact will appear directly in your conversation, typically below or beside Claude's text response.

## Step 3 — View the generated artifact
Once you've sent your prompt, Claude will process your request and display the result. The finished letter, document, or other content will appear directly in the conversation, formatted neatly in its own section. This is your live preview. You can scroll through the content, copy specific sections, or download it directly from this view.

**If it looks different:** Sometimes Claude might take a little longer to generate, especially for more complex requests. Just be patient. If it creates a text-only response in the chat and no formatted artifact, try rephrasing to be more specific about the format you want.

**💬 Example:** Below Claude's message, you now see a document titled "Thank-You Letter to Emma," complete with paragraphs of text as you requested, neatly formatted and separate from Claude's chat message.

**You'll know it worked when** the thank-you letter appears neatly formatted in its own section of the conversation, separate from the chat text. You'll see tools like "Copy" or "Download" directly above or below the artifact.

## Step 4 — Use the live preview to see changes instantly
One of the most powerful features of Artifacts is the **live preview**. This means that if you want to tweak or refine your creation, you don't have to generate a whole new artifact. Simply send a follow-up prompt in the chat. Claude will then modify the existing artifact, and you'll see the changes refresh in the same place.

**If it looks different:** If your follow-up prompt is significantly different from the first, Claude might create a *second* artifact alongside the first one. This is also perfectly normal and useful for comparing different versions of your work side-by-side.

**💬 Example:**
```
Now make a separate artifact that summarises the key points of this article: https://example.com/article
```
(Note: You can replace `https://example.com/article` with a real article URL.) Claude will create a second artifact, a concise bullet-point summary, shown below or beside your original letter.

**You'll know it worked when** your existing artifact updates with the new detail, or a new, separate artifact appears if your prompt asked for something entirely different. You'll see the content change in the artifact section without having to click anything extra.

## Common mistakes
-   **Not explicitly asking for a visual or formatted output:** While Claude is smart, sometimes it needs a clear hint. If you just ask "write a letter," it might give you text in the chat. **Fix:** Use words like "create a letter," "generate a document," or "make an artifact" to signal you want a formatted result.
-   **Forgetting to save or copy the artifact:** The Artifacts view shows your work directly in the conversation. While it stays with that specific chat, if you close the browser tab or start a new chat, your creation won't be saved automatically. **Fix:** Look for the "Copy" or "Download" buttons that appear near the artifact and use them to save your work to your computer.
-   **Not being specific enough in your request:** Vague prompts may produce text-only responses. **Fix:** Be clear about what you want — for example, specify the format ("make it a bullet-point list") or style ("use a professional tone").

## What this means for you
-   **In everyday life:** You can quickly draft various personal documents like thank-you notes, grocery lists, holiday packing lists, or even simple travel itineraries. Seeing them instantly formatted in the Artifacts section saves you time on typing and layout, letting you focus on the content.
-   **For your business or work:** This feature can be a real time-saver for professionals. You can produce meeting minutes, project briefs, or a basic calculator app (if you know a little HTML) without opening separate software. Just ask Claude, get the artifact, and then export it to share with colleagues.
-   **If you're just getting started:** The easiest first move is to ask Claude for a one-page summary of a recent email you received or a short article you're reading. You'll see the preview appear and quickly grasp the workflow in under five minutes.

## Try it now
Open Claude and type:
```
Create a short thank-you note artifact for a friend who baked me a delicious cake. Keep it under 100 words and make it sound very grateful.
```
Press enter and watch the document appear in your conversation. You'll have a finished piece in less time than it takes to brew a fresh cup of tea.
